To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HIV-infected mothers in Zambia present late in pregnancy and are less likely than HIV-uninfected women to receive antenatal care and well-baby and PMTCT of HIV care and services, and (2) the cost of antenatal and PMTCT care and services for HIV-infected mothers and their infants was $88 in 2011 US dollars and increased to $186 when triple-drug ART was included.

HIV-infected women present to antenatal care late and are lost to follow-up postpartum; HIV-uninfected babies receive fewer well-baby services than HIV-infected babies; and the cost of Option A services for HIV-infected mother/baby pairs is $88 and increases to $185 when the cost of antiretrovial therapy (ART) is included.
HIV-infected pregnant women in Zambia present to care late and many are lost after the delivery of their babies, and HIV-exposed babies receive more services than HIV-unexposured babies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uptake of HIV/AIDS services by pregnant women and their children in Zambia.
the uptake and outcomes of antenatal care, well-baby services, and PMTCH services in Zambia.
the uptake, outcomes and costs of antiretrovial treatment and prevention of mother-to child-transmission of HIV services under routine care condition in Zambia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the costs of PMTCT and ART services are higher in Option B+ compared to Option A.
Option B+ will increase costs of HIV care in Zambia, but the extent to which it will increase costs will depend on the extent to which the country is able to improve retention in care.
the costs and benefits of Option A in Zambia are unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the uptake and outcomes of antenatal care services were low, and that the uptake and retention of PMTCT services were also low and that the costs of providing PMTCT services are substantial and would increase with the implementation of Option B+.
the costs for Option A are high and Option B+ will cost more.
we have demonstrated that the costs for Option B+ are lower than Option A, and that Option B+ is more effective in preventing HIV transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to do more to retain women in care and ensure that they receive guideline concordant services, and that we need to move to Option B+.
we need to do more to improve PMTCT services in Zambia.
the costs of PMTCT services in Zambia are low.
